approachQuestion.prompt:
Occupied positions on a test strip

A strip has U unit slots numbered 0 through U−1. Each of n unsorted reservations [a,b) occupies the integer slots a,a+1,...,b−1. Return how many slots are occupied by at least one reservation. Duplicate reservations do not occupy a slot twice. Do not modify the input.

Input: U = 6, reservations = [[0,3],[2,5],[4,6],[2,5],[0,1],[5,6]]
Output: 6

Input: U = 3, reservations = [[0,1],[0,1],[2,3]]
Output: 2

Constraints: 1 ≤ U ≤ n ≤ 200000; 0 ≤ a < b ≤ U. Endpoint indexing and integer arithmetic take constant time. The relation U ≤ n is guaranteed. Among methods with best worst-case time under these constraints, minimize auxiliary memory.

options.text: Allocate U+1 zero counters. For each [a,b), add 1 at a and subtract 1 at b. Scan slots 0 through U−1 while accumulating the counters; count slots whose running total is positive.
options.feedback: Each range changes occupancy only at its two boundaries. Prefix accumulation reconstructs the number of reservations covering each slot; positivity, rather than the count itself, decides occupied slots.

options.text: Allocate U Boolean marks. For every reservation, loop through all its slots and mark them; count marked slots.
options.feedback: This returns the right count, but a reservation may cover the whole strip. Repeating per-slot work for n long reservations ignores the two-boundary representation.

options.text: Return the sum of b−a over all reservations, capped at U.
options.feedback: For U=3 and reservations [[0,1],[0,1],[0,1]], it returns 3 but only slot 0 is occupied, so the answer is 1. Capping does not repair overlap double-counting.

options.text: Use a difference array, but subtract at b+1, allocating U+2 counters, then count positive slots in 0 through U−1.
options.feedback: For U=2 and reservations [[0,1],[0,1]], this incorrectly occupies slot 1 as well. The half-open end b is the first excluded slot.

feedback.reason: Exploit a genuinely bounded dense domain with boundary differences instead of expanding every reservation.
details: Initialize U+1 integer counters to zero, apply two updates per reservation, then scan U slots with a running coverage count and occupied-slot total. No sorting or per-reservation slot loop is used.

Difference counters store occupancy changes, not occupied slots themselves. Apply each slot's event before testing running coverage. Dense initialization depends on U even when there are very few reservations.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For slot-differences, express the tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary space in n and U, including initialization of the counters. Remember U ≤ n.
constraints: Analyze only the named method. Count all temporary arrays and the call stack; exclude the supplied input and returned output. Numeric comparisons, assignments and arithmetic take constant time, with no overflow.
No hashing or amortized data structure is used. All loops and binary searches are iterative; there is no recursive stack.

options.text: Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(n)

feedback.reason: Initialize and scan U counters and apply two updates per reservation.
details: Initializing and scanning the dense counters costs O(U); two updates for each reservation cost O(n). The counter array takes O(U) auxiliary space. Since U≤n, total time is also O(n); the first option states the same bound explicitly in both sizes. Per-slot marking can repeat U work for each range.
Dense unit-slot domain, U≤n; zero initialization counted; direct constant-time indexing.
“Time O(nU), auxiliary space O(U)”: Every reservation makes only two updates, rather than updating every slot. Initialization and the one prefix scan add U work.
“Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(n)”: No comparison sorting or n-element record copy occurs. The specified memory is the dense U+1 counter array.
“Time O(n), auxiliary space O(1)”: The U≤n guarantee makes time linear in n, but the U+1 counters still occupy O(U), not constant memory.
